title: Affine mate calculation for the fixed tensor model
statement: Let R,A,R',A' be commutative rings with R-algebra structures on A,R' and a structure map A tensor_R R' to A'. Let phi_g':A to A' and phi_f':R' to A' be its restrictions and assume their spectrum square is cartesian. Let M be an A-K-flat unbounded complex, K a quasi-coherent derived object on Spec A, e:Q(tilde M) isomorphic to K, L=Lg'^*K quasi-coherent and its counit on tilde M invertible. For the fixed library tensor model m=ModuleCat.baseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R A R' M A' and any integer i, use the explicit U and a of [def-pc-affine-base-change-tilde-coordinates] with canonical target coordinate b. There exist a natural affine direct-image cohomology presentation d:Gamma H^i(-), restricted to R' and associated sheaf, isomorphic to H^i(Rf'_*(-)), and eU:tilde(restrict_R' U) isomorphic to H^i(Lg^*Rf_*K), with eU.hom followed by cohomology of the canonical base-change mate equal to tilde(restrict_R' a) followed by d at L. No stalk or localization conclusion is asserted. The universal comparison between arbitrary tensor models is not part of this fixed-model calculation.

source.place: Independence of choices for derived change of rings; affine base-change cohomology calculation

proof.text: The standard affine fibre-product isomorphism and its two projection equations identify Spec of the tensor-algebra structure map with the unique map between the two pullback cones. It is invertible; full faithfulness of Spec reflects this to an isomorphism of rings. Restriction along this ring equivalence is an equivalence of module categories, so the extension/restriction unit at m.cohomology(i) is invertible. Restrict to R′ and transport through hφf′ to obtain the invertible map t from unextended to extended source cohomology. This is the proved private helper tensorAlgebraMap_isIso and the unit argument in Lean.

Apply the ordinary affine mate theorem to the commuting equation sq.w. It provides d and eC with the square for the map c defined from m.comparison and homology of the ordinary coefficient map. Its source is the unextended tensor cohomology, and its theorem does not assume that the square is cartesian.

Naturality of the restriction-of-scalars comparison and m.localized_eq give t followed by restriction of a equal to c. Define eU as tilde of the inverse of t followed by eC. Apply tilde functoriality to the preceding identity and cancel inverse(t) followed by t. This yields the unchanged target square. All maps and equalities in this step are written explicitly in Lean.

proof_origin.place: Affine computation: tensor-algebra identification and extension/restriction adjunction
proof_origin.note: Lean proves cartesian coefficient invertibility, normalized source transport, localized_eq compatibility and final cancellation; ordinary affine mate isolated in one new theorem.
